fact: Presidential Decree 60/21 of 10 March 2021, the fee regulation of Angola's data protection agency (APD), lists an act of authorisation for international data transfer at a fee of Kz 350,450, so the APD's permission was a condition for sending personal data abroad; the document gives no date of effect other than its publication date, 2021-03-10.
system: Regulamento das Taxas da Agência de Protecção de Dados (Tabela de Taxas da APD, item 1.7 Transferência internacional de dados)

fact: Hunton reports that Angola's National Assembly passed Law 22/11 on 17 June 2011, under which the Data Protection Agency must approve international transfers to countries without adequate protection and controllers notify it of transfers to adequate countries; the note does not say when the law took effect.
source_slug: 2011-09-19 Angola Passes Personal Data Protection Law (Law 22-11)

fact: Lei n.º 22/11, arts 33-34, makes transfer of personal data abroad to a country with adequate protection subject to notification to the APD, and to a country without it subject to APD authorisation on stated grounds such as the data subject's written consent; art. 67 puts the law in force on publication, 17 June 2011.
system: Lei n.º 22/11 da Protecção de Dados Pessoais

fact: The APD fined Crescer Tech US$505,000 in 2026 for failing to notify and obtain authorisation for the international transfer of personal data to a cloud located abroad.

Valor Económico reported on 26 June 2026 that the APD fined Crescer Tech about USD 505,000 (c. 549 million kwanzas) for no notification or prior authorisation and an unauthorised international transfer to foreign cloud servers, and Fast Digital Center USD 112,000 (c. 110 million kwanzas) for inadequate security measures and no notification; deliberation dates are not given, so the publication date is used.
PTI reports the authority fined a company for failing to notify it and obtain authorisation for an international transfer of personal data, so a rule requiring authorisation is in force.

fact: Presidential Decree 275/20 of 21 October 2020 (Article 19) requires private credit information bureaux to have their primary data processing centres in national territory and replica facilities for data recovery also inside national territory, at least 30 km from the primary centre (Article 20); the document gives no later compliance date and no repeal.
